newsitem.title: CUBA: U.S. returns three illegal migrants to Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. returns three illegal migrants to Cuba.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard on Saturday returned to Cuba three people intercepted trying to emigrate illegally to the United States, the official Cuban news agency AIN said.
The handover took place just days before Cuban and U.S. officials were due to hold a new round of immigration talks.
There were no details immediately available on who the three Cuban migrants were.

The talks, to start in Havana on Wednesday, will be the first official public contact between the two countries since the re-election of President Bill Clinton. The officials were expected to review the progress of existing bilateral immigration accords.
AIN said the latest return of illegal Cuban immigrants by the U.S. authorities reflected the continuing validity of the immigration accords, signed in September 1994 and May 1995.
The three people handed back on Saturday came from Matanzas Province and had tried to reach the U.S. in a small boat. They would be returned to their homes after medical checks, AIN said.

Over the last 18 months, U.S. authorities have so far handed back 504 Cubans intercepted either trying to cross the Florida Straits or after entering the U.S. naval base at Guantanamo Bay in the east of the communist-ruled island.
The immigration accords were agreed after the so-called Cuban rafters' crisis of the summer of 1994 and were aimed at stemming the flow of Cubans trying to enter the United States illegally.

They are a rare example of bilateral cooperation between Cuba and its superpower neighbour, whose relations have been characterised by hostility for more than three decades. The two nations do not have normal diplomatic ties and Washington maintains a 35-year-old economic embargo against Cuba.
